key_insight: This paper shifts multimodal clinical diagnosis from accuracy-focused prompting to ranking-aware optimization, using AUROC as the target metric. The core idea is that better clinical prompts should rank true cases above false ones, especially when classes are highly imbalanced.
problem_solved: It addresses the mismatch between standard accuracy-based optimization and the realities of clinical data, where majority-class predictions can look strong on paper but fail in practice. The paper tackles how to optimize prompts for MLLMs in a way that improves clinically meaningful discrimination under class imbalance.
method: Evaluates multimodal large language models using AUROC instead of accuracy to better reflect clinical ranking performance.
Introduces ranking-aware prompt optimization for improving how prompts separate positive from negative cases.
Focuses on reflective prompt methods adapted to optimize for threshold-free diagnostic discrimination rather than majority-class correctness.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights that the choice of evaluation metric can completely change what counts as a good model in healthcare. It provides a more clinically aligned path for prompt optimization in MLLMs, especially for imbalanced diagnostic tasks.
visual_elements: A side-by-side comparison of accuracy vs. AUROC on imbalanced clinical data
A ranking diagram showing positives scored above negatives
A prompt optimization pipeline for multimodal diagnosis
An icon-based illustration of class imbalance and why majority prediction can be misleading
paper_title: Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization for Multimodal Clinical Diagnosis
paper_authors: Tian Xia, Minghao Liu, Yiqing Liang, Laixi Shi, Jiayun Wang
